title: Trump University Fraud 'Playbook' Released by Court Order
description_short: Trump University Fraud 'Playbook' Released by Court Order
description_medium: In June 2016, a federal judge ordered the release of Trump University's internal sales playbook, a detailed manual instructing salespeople to exploit students' financial insecurities, push them to use retirement savings, and upsell from $1,500 seminars to $35,000 'Gold Elite' packages. The playbook included scripts for overcoming objections about affordability and instructions not to let students think overnight before signing. Former instructors testified they were real estate agents with no particular expertise. The release severely damaged Trump's campaign and was used extensively by political opponents throughout the election.
description_long:
In June 2016, a federal judge ordered the release of Trump University's internal sales playbook, a detailed manual instructing salespeople to exploit students' financial insecurities, push them to use retirement savings, and upsell from $1,500 seminars to $35,000 'Gold Elite' packages. The playbook included scripts for overcoming objections about affordability and instructions not to let students think overnight before signing. Former instructors testified they were real estate agents with no particular expertise. The release severely damaged Trump's campaign and was used extensively by political opponents throughout the election.

The documents made sales methods visible in the litigation rather than leaving the dispute solely to competing public descriptions of the school. The contrast between educational promises and instructions about affordability is the central issue in the supplied account. A manual and former instructors' testimony are different forms of evidence and should remain identified as such. Their release was not itself a judgment on every student's experience or a final ruling on all fraud allegations.

title: Trump Fires Entire NLRB Board, Killing Worker Protections
description_short: Trump Fires Entire NLRB Board, Killing Worker Protections
description_medium: In late February 2025, Trump fired all sitting members of the National Labor Relations Board, leaving the agency without a quorum and unable to function. The NLRB is an independent agency established by Congress to protect workers' rights to organize. Legal scholars immediately noted NLRB board members have statutory protections against removal except for cause. The firings effectively rendered the agency inoperative, leaving millions of pending worker complaints unaddressed. The move was widely seen as a direct gift to large corporations and a declaration of war on organized labor.
notes: The source title identifies removal of a Democratic member, while the preserved text says all sitting NLRB members were fired and millions of complaints remained pending. Needs context to resolve scope.

title: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act: $1.5T Cut Skewed to Corporations
description_short: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act: $1.5T Cut Skewed to Corporations
description_medium: On December 22, 2017, President Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, overhauling the tax code with a sweeping $1.5 trillion tax cut. The legislation permanently slashed the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%, heavily favoring wealthy individuals and large corporations over middle-class taxpayers. While Republicans promised the cuts would pay for themselves through economic growth, the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office projected it would dramatically inflate the national deficit. The massive wealth transfer epitomized the administration's economic priorities, largely ignoring the working-class voters who helped elect Trump.
description_long:
On December 22, 2017, President Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, overhauling the tax code with a sweeping $1.5 trillion tax cut. The legislation permanently slashed the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%, heavily favoring wealthy individuals and large corporations over middle-class taxpayers. While Republicans promised the cuts would pay for themselves through economic growth, the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office projected it would dramatically inflate the national deficit. The massive wealth transfer epitomized the administration's economic priorities, largely ignoring the working-class voters who helped elect Trump.

The permanent reduction in the corporate rate was a concrete change to the tax system, whereas claims about growth financing the cuts were predictions about future economic behavior. The supplied account places those predictions alongside the CBO's deficit projection. Distributional criticism concerns who received tax relief; the budget criticism concerns federal revenue and spending over time. Neither question is resolved by labeling the bill a tax cut alone, and projections should not be confused with measured outcomes.

title: Russian IRA Troll Farms Run Massive US Election Interference Operation
description_short: Russian IRA Troll Farms Run Massive US Election Interference Operation
description_medium: Throughout 2016, Russia's Internet Research Agency (IRA), a St. Petersburg operation funded by Kremlin-linked oligarch Yevgeny Prigozhin, deployed hundreds of operatives creating thousands of fake American social media accounts across Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and YouTube, reaching an estimated 126 million Americans on Facebook alone. The IRA organized both pro-Trump rallies and fake progressive protests designed to suppress minority turnout. Mueller's February 2018 indictment charged 13 Russian nationals and 3 entities with conspiracy to defraud the United States. The operation constituted the most extensive foreign interference in American electoral history.
description_long:
Throughout 2016, Russia's Internet Research Agency (IRA), a St. Petersburg operation funded by Kremlin-linked oligarch Yevgeny Prigozhin, deployed hundreds of operatives creating thousands of fake American social media accounts across Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and YouTube, reaching an estimated 126 million Americans on Facebook alone. The IRA organized both pro-Trump rallies and fake progressive protests designed to suppress minority turnout. Mueller's February 2018 indictment charged 13 Russian nationals and 3 entities with conspiracy to defraud the United States. The operation constituted the most extensive foreign interference in American electoral history.

The indictment describes a covert influence operation using fabricated American identities, allowing foreign operatives to participate in political debate while obscuring their origin. The alleged conspiracy and the operation's reach are separate from any finding that it changed enough votes to determine the election. The charge against Russian individuals and entities also does not, by itself, establish that a U.S. campaign directed their conduct. Those distinctions preserve the significance of the interference without asserting an unproved electoral outcome.

title: Legal experts warn Trump DOJ leak policy could expose journalists to Espionage Act prosecution
description_short: Legal experts warn Trump DOJ leak policy could expose journalists to Espionage Act prosecution
description_medium: After Attorney General Pam Bondi revised Justice Department leak-investigation policy in April 2025, press-freedom lawyers warned that reporters who solicit or publish classified information could face heightened investigative risk, including possible Espionage Act prosecution. At a July 1 National Press Club event, attorneys Abbe Lowell and Mark Zaid advised journalists to prepare for such cases. The stronger claim that the administration had already chosen or was actively seeking a specific reporter as an Espionage Act test case, and the attributed private Trump quotation, should not be stated without direct corroboration.
description_long:
After Attorney General Pam Bondi revised Justice Department leak-investigation policy in April 2025, press-freedom lawyers warned that reporters who solicit or publish classified information could face heightened investigative risk, including possible Espionage Act prosecution. At a July 1 National Press Club event, attorneys Abbe Lowell and Mark Zaid advised journalists to prepare for such cases. The stronger claim that the administration had already chosen or was actively seeking a specific reporter as an Espionage Act test case, and the attributed private Trump quotation, should not be stated without direct corroboration.

The warning was prospective. Lowell and Zaid were discussing the exposure journalists could face under a changed investigative policy, rather than announcing that a reporter had already been convicted or selected for prosecution. The distinction matters because reporting on classified material and government efforts to identify a leak can intersect without proving that every journalist involved committed an offense. The supplied correction limits this entry to the policy change and attorneys' expressed concerns about its potential application.

title: Trump Revokes 3,000+ International Student Visas in Mass Purge Campaign

title: Michael Cohen Office Raided by FBI
description_short: Michael Cohen Office Raided by FBI
description_medium: On April 9, 2018, the FBI executed search warrants on the office, hotel room, and home of Michael Cohen, President Trump's long-time personal lawyer and 'fixer.' Agents seized millions of documents, emails, and electronic devices, seeking evidence related to bank fraud, wire fraud, and illicit campaign contributions, particularly regarding hush-money payments made to Stormy Daniels. The unprecedented raid enraged Trump, who tweeted that 'Attorney-Client privilege is dead!' The seizure ultimately provided the crucial evidence that forced Cohen to plead guilty and explicitly implicate Trump in directing illegal campaign finance schemes.
description_long:
On April 9, 2018, the FBI executed search warrants on the office, hotel room, and home of Michael Cohen, President Trump's long-time personal lawyer and 'fixer.' Agents seized millions of documents, emails, and electronic devices, seeking evidence related to bank fraud, wire fraud, and illicit campaign contributions, particularly regarding hush-money payments made to Stormy Daniels. The unprecedented raid enraged Trump, who tweeted that 'Attorney-Client privilege is dead!' The seizure ultimately provided the crucial evidence that forced Cohen to plead guilty and explicitly implicate Trump in directing illegal campaign finance schemes.

The search was an evidence-gathering step conducted under warrants, distinct from a guilty plea or trial verdict. Cohen's position as Trump's personal lawyer made the seizure politically consequential, but attorney-client protections did not automatically settle the legality of every item investigators obtained. The account links the search to later campaign-finance admissions while describing Trump's reaction at the time. The entry should therefore be read as a chronological investigative development, not proof that every seized communication reflected unlawful conduct.

title: Comey Letter Reopens Clinton Email Probe 11 Days Before Election
description_short: Comey Letter Reopens Clinton Email Probe 11 Days Before Election
description_medium: On October 28, 2016, FBI Director James Comey sent Congress a letter announcing he was reopening the investigation into Hillary Clinton's private email server after agents discovered emails on a laptop belonging to Anthony Weiner, husband of Clinton aide Huma Abedin. Comey closed the investigation again November 6, two days before the election, finding nothing new. Statistical analyses suggested the letter significantly shifted polling against Clinton in the final stretch.
description_long:
On October 28, 2016, FBI Director James Comey sent Congress a letter announcing he was reopening the investigation into Hillary Clinton's private email server after agents discovered emails on a laptop belonging to Anthony Weiner, husband of Clinton aide Huma Abedin. Comey closed the investigation again November 6, two days before the election, finding nothing new. Statistical analyses suggested the letter significantly shifted polling against Clinton in the final stretch. Former DOJ officials from both parties widely criticized the norm-breaking disclosure; Comey himself later expressed regret about the letter's electoral impact.

The proximity to voting made the announcement unusually consequential, because voters received notice of renewed investigative activity before its significance had been established. Comey's later statement that investigators found nothing new is part of the same sequence and limits what the first letter demonstrated. The existence of additional emails did not itself establish fresh wrongdoing by Clinton. Polling analyses discussed in the account address possible electoral effects, which should remain estimates rather than a proven explanation for the result.

title: Wire Services AP, Reuters, Bloomberg Stripped of Permanent Press Pool Slot
description_short: Wire Services AP, Reuters, Bloomberg Stripped of Permanent Press Pool Slot
description_medium: On April 15, 2025, the White House announced that AP, Reuters, and Bloomberg News — wire services that together reach billions of readers — would lose their permanent reserved spot in the daily presidential press pool. The move came one week after a federal judge ruled in the AP's favor in its lawsuit over access, and was widely seen as a workaround to evade the court order.
description_long:
On April 15, 2025, the White House announced that AP, Reuters, and Bloomberg News — wire services that together reach billions of readers — would lose their permanent reserved spot in the daily presidential press pool. The move came one week after a federal judge ruled in the AP's favor in its lawsuit over access, and was widely seen as a workaround to evade the court order. The AP filed an emergency motion on April 16 arguing the new policy violated the ruling by still giving the administration sole discretion over access.

A permanent pool position differs from access granted occasionally at the administration's discretion. The change therefore affected the reliability of wire-service coverage, even if it did not ban every wire-service reporter from every presidential event. The AP's filing characterized the revised arrangement as inconsistent with the court ruling; that allegation should remain separate from a subsequent judicial finding. The sequence illustrates a dispute over implementation of press-access protections rather than a completed resolution of the lawsuit.
